questions.prompt: What comes from Glimmer's mouth on the first day of practice?
questions.evidenceText: On the first day: a small puff of smoke. Just smoke. No fire at all.

questions.prompt: What makes Glimmer rush toward the Fog Marsh fox?
choices: The fox has found Fern's precious seeds.
The fox has challenged Glimmer to a race.
The fox has brought Glimmer a cinnamon leaf.
questions.answer: The fox has found Fern's precious seeds.
questions.evidenceText: That evening, a Fog Marsh fox came creeping into Moonwood. It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.

questions.prompt: What lesson does Glimmer's first real fire teach?
choices: Practice and a strong reason can bring out a new skill.
Spark's advice made Glimmer's fire appear at once.
Practising alone at the stream caused the final flame.
questions.answer: Practice and a strong reason can bring out a new skill.
questions.rationale: Glimmer practised fire breathing every morning, then protecting Fern's precious seeds gave them a reason to really mean it; this shows practice and a strong reason can bring out a new skill.
questions.evidenceText: The fire had been inside all along. "I just needed to really mean it."

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: Every morning, Glimmer practised. Fire breathing was the most important thing a dragon could do. And Glimmer could not do it yet.
It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.
